notes: The Vitamix 5200 base has a motor of about 2 peak output horsepower, with an On/Off switch, a High/Variable switch and a variable speed dial; the manual rates the machine 120 V, 50/60 Hz, 11.5 A. The manual also covers 220/240 V machines, which have a reset button on the bottom, and the drive socket is a separate replaceable part (iFixit guide).

gaps: The first-cited vitamix.com file (154276_5200_Owners_Manual.pdf) has Professional Series 200 on its cover and never names the 5200, so it was not used. Claims were re-sourced to the Vitamix 5200 Owner's Manual (103670, 7/13), which names the 5200.
That file also gives different dimensions on its specification page than the 5200 manual, so it is another model's manual.
The Certified Reconditioned - Standard manual (154275) does not name the 5200 and gives the same dimensions as the Professional Series 200 manual, so its parts diagram claims were left out.

The 5200 manual gives about 2 peak output horsepower under Motor and 120 V, 50/60 Hz, 11.5 A under a separate Electrical heading; it gives no watt figure, so no w is set, and the electrical figures are kept in notes as the machine's rating, not the motor's.
The manual does not name the motor type, so motor_universal is the nearest template type.
The manual says the motor protects itself from overheating (on 120 V machines, switch off for up to 45 minutes to reset) but names no part, so no thermostat is claimed.
No triac, control board or speed control circuit is named in the manual, so no thyristor claim is made.
No OEM part numbers are given for the drive socket, the switches or the dial.
The manual does not say what electrical type the speed dial is; it is filed under potentiometer as the nearest template type.
method: Vitamix 5200 Owner's Manual, 103670 7/13 (vitamix.com/assets/manuals/ca/5200-owners-manual.pdf, 20 pages, linked as '5200' on Vitamix's manuals page): PDF pages 7 (power cord), 10 (control panel) and 20 (specifications, headed Vitamix 5200). Read as text.

iFixit guide 165463, Vitamix 5200 Drive Socket Replacement, read through the iFixit API (/api/2.0/guides/165463). The guide lists no parts, and the drive socket claim rests on its steps and tool list.
The vitamix.com files 154276_5200_Owners_Manual.pdf and 154275_5200_Recon.pdf were read but are not used (see gaps).
Vitamix's troubleshooting FAQ returned HTTP 404 at two locale URLs for the researcher and was not used.
The researcher found no 5200 motor teardown; a Williams-Sonoma PDF returned by that search did not show Vitamix text and was not used.

comps.spec: Base motor of about 2 peak output horsepower (specifications page).
On/Off switch: push up for on, push down for off.
High/Variable switch. High is the fastest speed; Variable activates the lower variable speeds and the speed dial. Set it to Variable before switching the machine on.
Variable speed dial, which selects the speed settings. It is active only when the High/Variable switch is on Variable.

Drive socket whose teeth engage the container blade, with a rubber jar pad around it. The iFixit guide loosens it with a 5/64 in Allen wrench through a small hole at its base and seats the new socket on the square nut.
Long power cord; the unused length is stored underneath the base and plastic cord retainers hold the cord.
